 Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5Pc3y Skip next section Zelenskyy lauds strength of Ukraine's battlefield positions 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Zelenskyy lauds strength of Ukraine's battlefield positions
 Jon Shelton Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Wednesday evening said his country's military is holding its own against Russian troops, as evidenced by Kyiv's defense of two towns in the Donetsk region despite Russian claims to have captured them. 
 Speaking to Ukrainians in his nightly video address, Zelenskyy said, "As ‌for the situation at the front, our ‌positions are strong. And although the Russians are making very ​intensive attempts to advance towards Dobropillia and Kostiantynivka, ⁠we ​are destroying the ​occupiers."
 Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5Pc1n Skip next section Russia planned false-flag 'provocation' in Poland near Kaliningrad — Polish media 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Russia planned false-flag 'provocation' in Poland near Kaliningrad — Polish media
 Saim Dušan Inayatullah Poland has heavily fortified its border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad since Moscow invaded neighboring Ukraine in 2022 Image: Attila Husejnow/ZUMA/IMAGO The Russian secret service planned to carry out an attack on sites in Polish territory near the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad , the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita reported, citing anonymous Polish security sources.
 The same sources said a simultaneous staged attack on Russian territory was also planned.
 In October, Poland carried out a large-scale security operation at the border with Kaliningrad, involving police, border police and the military.
 At the time, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Polish intelligence had provided information that pointed to the possible entry of armed individuals on Polish territory.
 Rzeczpospolita reported that the operation successfully thwarted the planned attack, which the anonymous sources said was to be pinned on Ukraine.
 The aim of the alleged Russian operation was to cause Poland to halt its support to Ukraine,
 Poland borders both Ukraine and the Russian territory of Kaliningrad and is one of Kyiv's most fervent supporters within the European Union.
 Intelligence Minister Tomasz Simoniak told the newspaper that there had been a "real threat," but Warsaw did not otherwise comment on the Rzeczpospolita report or confirm or deny the claims that the October operation was carried out in response to Russian provocation. 
 Earlier this year, US media reported that US intelligence had indicated Russia could attempt to test NATO's resolve through a limited attack on a member of the alliance or by sending soldiers in unmarked uniforms onto NATO territory.
 Edited by: Sean Sinico https://p.dw.com/p/5PbFL Skip next section Ukraine's top diplomat calls for 'pressure' on Russia at trilateral talks 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Ukraine's top diplomat calls for 'pressure' on Russia at trilateral talks
 Trump greeted Putin and Xi in Shenzhen ahead of their much anticipated meeting on Thursday Image: Iori Sagisawa/REUTERS Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha has urged China and the United States to apply ‌pressure ⁠on ⁠ Russia to end its war in Ukraine.
 "Both the United States and China have a decisive influence on Russia, especially in the context of ending the aggression, ending the war. We hope and expect that this will be the tone adopted in this conversation: pressure on Russia to end the war,"  Sybiha told reporters.
 China's ​President Xi Jinping, US President ​Donald Trump and Russian President ​Vladimir ‌Putin are set to hold a trilateral talks on ‌Thursday in China's southern ‌city ​of Shenzhen.
 Follow DW's coverage of the events running up to the trilateral meeting here .
 Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5PakR Skip next section At least 4 killed in Russian strikes in Odesa 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 At least 4 killed in Russian strikes in Odesa
 Regional officials say that at least four people have been killed in Russian strikes in the Black Sea port city of Odesa.
 Regional governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram that ‌at least 13 people ‌had also ​been injured.
 Kiper said windows of residential buildings, cafes and shops ​had been broken, a car had been ⁠set on ​fire and several ​other vehicles had been ​damaged.
 Both Russia and Ukraine have increased their use of long-range missiles, along with the continued use of drones, to strike inside each other's territories.
 Odesa is a frequent target of Russian missile and drone strikes.
 Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5PaVK Skip next section EU proposes €45 billion additional support for Ukraine in 2027 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 EU proposes €45 billion additional support for Ukraine in 2027
 The European Commission has proposed a further €45 billion ($49.3 billion) in additional financial support to Ukraine in 2027.
 "For 2026, Ukraine's needs are covered. And today we are proposing a further €45 billion to cover two thirds of its needs for 2027," European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said.
 "Together, with our international partners, we will strengthen Ukraine. For as long as it takes to achieve a just and lasting peace," von der Leyen said. 
 According to the Commission, the proposed support would have up to €25 billion allocated to military support and up to €20 billion as general budget support in Ukraine.
 The EU and member states have provided nearly €238 billion in support to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022.
 Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5PaOM Skip next section Germany calls for Russia to be held accountable after chemical weapons probe 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Germany calls for Russia to be held accountable after chemical weapons probe
 Germany's Foreign Office has called for Russia to be held accountable after a Ukrainian investigation concluded that Russia had used CS gas on Ukrainian forces.
 "Russia continues its relentless war against Ukraine and commits grave breaches of the Chemical Weapons Convention," the Foreign Office said in a post on X.
 "A Ukrainian investigation has found clear evidence of the use of prohibited chemicals. Russia needs to be held accountable," the statement read. 
 The Ukrainian probe was conducted with the help of the global chemical weapons watchdog, the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW).
 The organization confirmed in 2024 that CS gas, which is banned on the battlefield, was found at several sites in Ukraine.
 The new investigation now links the weapons used to the Russian military.
 Ukraine focused on an incident from September 2024, in which Russian forces attacked a military post in central Ukraine.
 Investigators found a video posted to a pro-Russian Telegram channel, which they say showed a grenade filled with tear gas being dropped from a drone onto Ukrainian forces.
 Russia is party to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC), having signed it in 1993 and ratified it in 1997.
 Use of riot control agents on the battlefield is prohibited under the CWC.

 Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5PZfv Skip next section Europe must be part of Ukraine peace talks — Wadephul 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Europe must be part of Ukraine peace talks — Wadephul
 Germany 's top diplomat is insisting that Europe should be involved in negotiations to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
 "I expect, and have no reason to doubt, that talks on Ukraine's future will be held between Russia and Ukraine with Europe's participation," Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said during a meeting with his Azerbaijani counterpart, Jeyhun Bayramov, in the capital Baku.
 Failing that, it would not be possible to achieve a sustainable solution that guarantees "that a new conflict does not emerge after this war, which we hope will end as soon as possible," Wadephul warned.
 The comments come ahead of a trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China on Thursday.
 Wadephul did welcome the planned trilateral talks in Shenzhen between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
 "Every conversation that takes place is a good conversation, I say as a foreign policy expert," he said.

 Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5PZft Skip next section Reports of two industrial facilities struck in Russia's Krasnodar region 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Reports of two industrial facilities struck in Russia's Krasnodar region
 Ukraine has reportedly struck two industrial targets in Russia 's Krasnodar region.
 Media outlets in Ukraine are reporting that oil refineries have been struck, although this cannot be independently verified.
 Telegram channels in the Krasnodar region warned of overnight drone strikes but it was not immediately clear what had been hit and whether damage had been caused.
 Ukrainian online publication The Kyiv Independent  reported that the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries had been hit and cited Telegram channel Exilenova, a pro-Ukrainian account that tracks developments in the ongoing war with the information.
 The two refineries are the largest in the region and have previously been targeted by drone strikes.
 The reported strikes come a day after Ukraine hit the Kerch bridge, linking occupied Crimea to Russia, putting the road and railway out of action.
 The Ukrainian General Staff said an arch and part of the bridge's road section collapsed into the water, severing the link for vehicular traffic, while the railway line was still standing but with a damaged arch.
 Edited by: Alex Berry https://p.dw.com/p/5PZfm Skip next section Welcome to our coverage 11/18/2026 November 18, 2026 Welcome to our coverage
 We're following the latest developments in Russia 's ongoing invasion of Ukraine .
 Ukraine has launched strikes on targets not far from the Kerch bridge, that up until yesterday, could be traveled by road and rail from the occupied Crimean peninsula to Russia's Krasnodar region.
 The bridge is an arterial route for both Russia's military and civilian supplies to Crimea and is seen by Ukraine as a symbol of Moscow's annexation of Crimea in 2014.
 There've also been more Russian overnight attacks, with Ukraine reporting dozens of interceptions.
 Stay with us as we bring you updates related to Russia's war in Ukraine .
